summary: Martin Haug worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth and at Bonn under Theodor Benfey, later holding posts at Bonn, Heidelberg, Deccan College, and Munich.

Martin Joachim Kümmel is a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed his MA and PhD at the University of Freiburg, studying under Eva Tichy, Helmut Rix, and others, and held a post at Jena.

Martin King Whyte worked in Sinology, studying at Cornell University (~1960–1964) and Harvard University (~1964–1971). He held academic posts at the University of Michigan (~1970–1994) and Harvard (~2000–2012).

Martin Lehnert works in Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Freiburg and held a post as Professor of East Asian Religion and Philosophy at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (attested 2016).

Martin Lowenthal works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche and Namkhai Norbu, and held posts at Boston College and Harvard University.

Martin Riesebrodt was a religious studies scholar who studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1970–1974) and Heidelberg University (~1974–1980). He held a post at the University of Chicago from ~1990 to 2014.

Martin Seeger is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under doctoral supervisor Barend Jan Terwiel by 2004. He also held a post at the University of Hamburg (attested 2004).

Martin T. Adam is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at McGill University under Richard P. Hayes (attested 2002) and also studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies with teachers including Kameshwar Nath Mishra.

Martin Willson was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. His education included studying under traditional teachers such as Thubten Yeshe, Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, Geshe Thubten Loden, Zasep Tulku Rinpoche, Geshe Rabten, Jampa Tegchok, and Geshe Lhundub Sopa.

Martina Draszczyk works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Lambert Schmithausen, completed her doctorate at the University of Vienna (attested 2012), and held a post at the University of Vienna.

Martino Dibeltulo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (attested 2015) under doctoral supervisor Donald S. Lopez Jr. and mentor Ester Bianchi.
Maruo Ujiie, a scholar in Buddhist studies, studied as a research student at Tribhuvan University (attested 1970) and served as a lecturer at Koyasan University (attested 1970).

Marvin Eisenberg was a history and archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1939–1943) and Princeton University (~1946–1952). He held a post at the University of Michigan from ~1949 to 1989.

Mary Clabaugh Wright was a scholar in Sinology and history/archaeology. She studied at Vassar College, Radcliffe College, and Harvard University (~1938–1951), and held an academic post at Yale University from ~1959 to 1970.
Mary Jaksch is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied at the University of Sunderland under Peter Harvey (attested 2007).

Marybeth White works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed a double major honors degree at York University and was a doctoral candidate at Wilfrid Laurier University (attested 2006).

Marylin Martin Rhie works in Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and Sinology. She studied under mentors Harrie Vanderstappen and Pramod Chandra, and held a post as professor at Smith College (attested 1986).

Masaaki Chikusa worked in Sinology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1949–1956), later becoming professor emeritus there (~1993), and held a post at Otani University (~1993–2001).

Masaaki Hattori is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Calcutta, and held main academic posts at Kyoto University, Osaka Prefecture University, and Osaka Gakuin University.

Masaaki Nitta is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1960–1967). He served as a professor at Fukui Prefectural University (attested 1983–1988) and Fukui Prefectural College (attested 1991).
